messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — proposal to change analytics.events schema. Thinking of adding a route_meta_id (uuid) and keeping a small denormalized route_cost float on the event row for fast console queries.

sam: Can you sketch why both? why not just join to route_metadata?

maria: perf. dashboards query 90M rows for last 30d. joins kill us. denorm gives consistent <100ms dashboard tiles. route_meta_id allows authoritative lookups when we need full metadata.

lucy: Also need customer_tier on queries for quota dashboards — more GROUP BYs. Denorm reduces cardinality pressure.

todd: Concern: drift. If we store route_cost on events, how do we handle price changes/discounts/rollouts?

anika: proposal: route_metadata table with (route_meta_id PK, route_id, customer_tier, cost_multiplier, effective_from, effective_to). Backfill events with the route_meta_id that was active at event time and copy computed route_cost. Future changes insert new route_metadata rows; no rewrite of old events.

sam: That seems fine. How big is the backfill? we have ~1.1B events in the last year. Backfill windowed + parallel jobs?

maria: plan: shadow-write route_meta_id + route_cost from API -> kafka while we run backfill for 6 months of high-traffic. Backfill job: run per-tenant partitions, 100k rows batches, idempotent upserts. Example SQL snippet: 

```
UPDATE analytics.events e
SET route_meta_id = rm.id, route_cost = rm.cost
FROM (
  SELECT id, cost FROM route_metadata WHERE route_id = e.route_id AND effective_from <= e.ts AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to > e.ts) LIMIT 1
) rm
WHERE e.route_meta_id IS NULL
LIMIT 100000;
```

lucy: we should avoid LIMIT in UPDATE style for PG; better do batch by pk-range. Also add job-state table to resume.

maria: agreed — we'll use chunked ranges on event_id and keep a migration progress table.

todd: indexes? we'll need index on (route_meta_id), (route_id, effective_from), and on (ts) for chunking. Also watch write amplification on replicas.

anika: console changes: routing/quotas dashboards need to switch to route_cost for aggregate token-costs. Add feature flag to flip dashboards to denorm fields. We'll keep join-based views for verification.

sam: rollback strategy?

maria: shadow-write only first. then backfill. deploy console behind FF. if we see >2% discrepancy between join-aggregates and denorm-aggregates during verification window, pause rollout and re-evaluate.

lucy: telemetry retention: historical recalculation required for policy changes (e.g., retroactive discounts). plan is to keep route_metadata effective ranges to support reprice re-ingestion jobs for selected windows, not whole-history rewrites.

devops-bot: migration-job scheduled: analytics.route_meta_backfill starting 2026-05-03T04:00:00Z, workers=16, throttling=5000 r/s.

anika: ops note: add new SLO for backfill jobs not to exceed DB I/O threshold — ops will kill if p99 latency > 400ms across replicas.

todd: testing: add unit tests for query planner paths, and a perf harness that runs the dashboard tile queries against a snapshot with denorm vs join. Early numbers: join median 480ms, denorm median 42ms in staging slice.

sam: any schema migration tool? we're using gh-ost for mysql but analytics is Postgres. We'll use online migrations via pg_repack-friendly pattern: create new columns nullable, backfill, add not-null constraint, then drop old.

maria: timeline: create table + columns (week 1), start shadow writes (week 2), incremental backfill 8 weeks (week 3-10), FF dashboards week 11, full flip week 13 if no issues.

lucy: don't forget to update retention/backfill docs and the console notes about interpretation of historical costs.

amika: tiny nit: name the column route_cost_units or route_cost_usd? currency confusion.

anika: use micros_usd (int64 micros) to avoid floating comparison issues. store cost_multiplier as rational? We'll pick micros_usd on event and multiplier as a decimal on metadata.
__note: This thread is a single Slack conversation string. No title field included as per agents.md.
